GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg|brace-expansion.notes: brace-expansion DoS via unbounded expansion length. REWRITTEN 2026-08-05 (§2.129); the previous note's conclusion was wrong. It claimed upstream 'backported nothing to the 1.x/2.x lines' and that the only exit was migrating eslint 8 -> 10. Upstream has since shipped 1.1.18, 2.1.4 and 5.0.9, so the per-major `overrides` in package.json pin every line, and the twenty advisory paths that note enumerated (eslint, @typescript-eslint, the electron-builder packaging chain, @sentry/vite-plugin, test-exclude) are ALL GONE. One node remains: `node_modules/npm/node_modules/brace-expansion`, marked `dev: true` and `inBundle: true` — the copy vendored inside the npm CLI that the `@semantic-release/npm` devDependency pulls in. npm declares 65 bundleDependencies, so a child `overrides` entry cannot reach inside the bundle. NOT UNFIXABLE, DELIBERATELY DEFERRED: overriding the top-level `npm` dependency to 12.0.2 would clear it, and that is rejected only because a major bump of the tool that publishes our releases is not worth a glob DoS in CI tooling. Unreachability rests on `dev` + `inBundle` + absence from the shipped bundle, NOT on `npm run audit:prod` — that script excludes devDependencies, and `undici` shows why it is no proof of shipped safety: it is a devDependency that vite bundles into the main process, so `audit:prod` does not cover code we actually ship. SCOPE, stated honestly: the key is package-scoped rather than chain-scoped because npm's v3 audit output gives nodes, not dependency chains, and audit-ci can only narrow to the package name. A FUTURE runtime path of brace-expansion would therefore also be suppressed until expiry; the 2026-11-01 date is the backstop that forces a re-look. Exit conditions: @semantic-release/npm moves off a vendored npm, or we take the npm 12 override.
